html:
Hassan Gouled Aptidon was the first president of Djibouti, leading it from independence on 27 June 1977 until 1999.

An Issa Somali, he had sat in the French parliament in Paris and led the campaign for independence after the referendum of 1967 kept the territory French. He kept Djibouti neutral between Somalia and Ethiopia, which were at war in the Ogaden in his first year, and close to France, which kept a large garrison.

He made his party the only legal one in 1981. Afar resentment of Issa rule led to the civil war of 1991. He handed power in 1999 to his chief of staff and relative Ismaïl Omar Guelleh.
sum: Hassan Gouled Aptidon was the first president of Djibouti, leading it from independence on 27 June 1977 until 1999.
